_comment: The achievement set a title's Live definition would have returned offline.
Titles enumerate the whole set - earned and unearned - to draw an achievements
screen, and the store on its own only ever holds what a title has awarded, so
a fresh install would otherwise hand back nothing.
This file is consulted first and is deliberately empty. Keys are now recovered
from the title's own assemblies at install by WPR.AchievementKeyMiner, which
reads 137 of the 171 XNA titles in the corpus - including all five this file
used to carry by hand, key for key.
Add a product here when mining cannot answer for it. Two kinds cannot:
a title whose keys the walk does not reach, and a title that reads its key
back off GamerServices.Achievement.Key and re-awards what this emulator handed
it - the second declares no key anywhere in its xap, so no walk will ever find
one. An install that mines nothing and still calls the achievement API logs a
warning naming the product, which is where the ones worth adding show up.
An entry wins over the mined set for that product, so adding one also freezes
it: a later miner improvement cannot correct a key written here. Prefer fixing
the miner where the shape is recoverable, and keep this for the shapes that
are not.
Only 'key' is required, and it has to be the exact string the title passes to
AwardAchievement - it is what the title indexes the set by. 'name',
'description' and 'gamerScore' are optional and exist because they are the one
thing mining cannot recover: no xap carries them, since the phone got them
from Live. Leave them out rather than guessing. An omitted name falls back to
the key, which is wrong to read but true; an invented one reads as fact.
The example below is not a real title and never matches one - the all-zero
product id is reserved for this illustration.

products.title: Example - not a real title, shown for the format only
products.source: Where the keys came from: the type and member they were read out of, so the next reader can check the claim rather than trust it
